This page in English El T-MEC tiene las disposiciones laborales más fuertes y de mayor alcance de cualquier tratado comercial. El tratado contiene un capítulo laboral que da prioridad a las obligaciones laborales, incluyéndolas en el núcleo del tratado y haciéndolas totalmente aplicables. Este cambio es uno importante en comparación con el TLCAN, que solo contenía un acuerdo paralelo sobre el ámbito laboral, y beneficiará enormemente a los trabajadores y empresas estadounidenses. Los Mirlos: Tiny Desk Concert September 17, 2026 10:00 AM ET Felix Contreras Credit: Photo: Vanessa Castillo/NPR From jazz and Tejano to norteño and ska, 'El Tiny' returns with a takeover from Sept. 15 to Oct. 15 for Latin Music Month . Originally born from Afro-Colombian communities, cumbia spread across the Spanish-speaking world , acquiring distinct musical accents along the way. In Peru, cumbia became particularly popular among oil workers deep in the Amazon. And when Jorge Rodriguez Grández started Los Mirlos in his small hometown of Moyobamba, his band played a regional style called cumbia amazónica, easily identifiable by its electric, reverb-heavy, surf-rock guitar. Sponsor Message Alt.Latino Cumbia: The Musical Backbone Of Latin America Los Mirlos' time behind the Desk is not only a joyful celebration of this music but also a trail of small towns and cities throughout the Amazon jungle. Throughout their performance, these cultural ambassadors share stories and declare their love for cumbia and their tropical homeland. We are so fortunate to host and share with you a group of true pioneers and innovators who, over 50 years later, still effortlessly pump out cumbia grooves. Los Texmaniacs ' music is a living history lesson. The conjunto sound is driven by the button accordion, a mid-19th century instrument that made its way to the U.S.-Mexico border by way of German, Czech and Polish immigrants. But this music is also just perfect for twirling on the dance floor to songs about true love, heartbreak, folk heroes and reflections on life. pages.text: Los Tigres' Tiny Desk, explained : Alt.Latino : NPR Accessibility links Skip to main content Keyboard shortcuts for audio player Los Tigres' Tiny Desk, explained : Alt.Latino Last week we published a Tiny Desk Concert that ended up being unusual for a few reasons. First of all, it was the final production of our sixth annual El Tiny series. This was a very emotional moment for a lot of reasons. People really love Los Tigres del Norte, to the point that playing their albums feels like sitting with family. And if you’ve seen the introduction I gave the band just before they played at the desk you can see that I wasn’t embarrassed to get emotional when I talked about what the band means to me. That emotional intro led to some changes in our process and format that resulted in a huge response from the audience that went viral. The result was a messy moment behind the scenes here at NPR and more than a little confusion for a lot of you. This week’s episode looks back at last week. First we want to share with you, directly from us, an explanation of what happened. But mostly we want to put the spotlight back on the band and their music because for decades they have been bringing out the kind emotions that got this whole thing started. Give it a listen and enjoy the music. Again. - Felix This podcast episode was produced by Noah Caldwell and edited by Jacob Ganz and Otis Hart. Suraya Mohamed is the executive producer of NPR Music. pages.text: Lou Piniella's case to be voted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame Skip to Content CINCINNATI -- Will this time finally be Lou Piniella 's turn? Once again, Piniella -- the longtime great manager -- is one of eight candidates on the Contemporary Baseball Era ballot for managers, executives and umpires, announced last week. A 16-member panel consisting of Hall of Fame players, Major League executives, media members and historians will consider each of the eight candidates, who must receive a minimum of 12 votes (at least 75%) to be elected. The results of the Class of 2027 ballot will be announced on Sunday, Dec. 6. Joining Piniella is some very steep competition of fellow managers and baseball executives. The list includes Sandy Alderson, Dusty Baker, Bruce Bochy, Joe Maddon, Brian Sabean, Ted Turner and Bill White.​ Piniella, 83, has come painfully close to election on two previous occasions only to fall one vote shy -- both times -- from getting the long-awaited call from Cooperstown. During a Major League managerial career with five clubs that spanned 23 seasons, Piniella posted a record of 1,835-1,713. He is ranked 17th all-time in wins. Of the 16 managers ahead of him, 12 are in the Hall of Fame. Two of those managers are Baker and Bochy. Piniella managed the Yankees (1986-88), Reds (1990-92), Mariners (1993-2002), Devil Rays (2003-05) and Cubs (2007-10). He has led his clubs to seven postseason appearances and helmed eight seasons of 90 or more victories with four different clubs. NPS Photo/Emily Mesner The story of Arctic archeology is dominated by one towering figure – J. Louis Giddings. A tall, soft-spoken man, he was nevertheless one of the loudest and most respected voices in his field. During his twenty-five years of fieldwork in Northwest Alaska, Giddings worked on five major excavations. He was instrumental in the identification of several previously unexplored cultures and the discovery of many of the most important sites in Arctic archeology. His work at the Cape Krusenstern beach ridges and Onion Portage formed the basis of the modern understanding of the human history in Arctic Alaska. This exhibition ‘Louvre Photo’ takes the Louvre as a model, a subject, a source of inspiration and a starting point for reinvention. Through more than 300 photos of the Louvre – its artworks, its exhibition galleries and its open spaces, as well as visitors both famous and anonymous, museum workers, hidden nooks and behind-the-scenes corridors – ‘Louvre Photo’ invites visitors to explore and uncover, taking a step back and offering a new look at the museum, the institution and its collections – sometimes with a touch of humour and subversiveness. ‘Louvre Photo’ covers the long period spanning from the invention of photography until today, from the first photographers to those invited to photograph the museum in modern times – most recently Robert Polidori.
